## Question
Labels (n), unlabeled records (N) and the predictor f are fixed; nominal coverage must hold.
**How much shorter than the best published valid interval (PPI++) can the interval be, and under which conditions is there no room?**
Target: the population mean E[Y] (shared by all nine ppi-python sets; truth known when a pool is the population).
Headline = mean. A regression-coefficient target is an *extension that does not start until the mean story
(tiers, regime map, theory check) is complete*; if anything is added first, it is a skewed continuous Y
(census_income, gene_expression) as a Wald stress test of the mean.

## Setup and the floor (to be proved in the paper; derivations below are elementary and checked by idea-review)
Z = information on every record (T1: f(X) only; T2: f(X) and X, and the alphafold PTM indicators; sets with no extra features are T1 only).
M = n+N records carry Z, n of them (a simple random subset) carry Y; labeling is MCAR with known propensity n/M.
Pooled estimator for a fixed g, h = Y − g(Z): θ̂_g = mean_{all M} g + mean_{lab} h = mean_all Y + [mean_lab h − mean_all h]. Hence
- **V(g) = Var(Y)/M + (1/n − 1/M)·Var(h)** (the two terms are uncorrelated: the first is fixed given the M units, the second is a mean-zero simple-random-sampling error). Minimised by g* = m(Z) = E[Y|Z]:
  **floor V* = σ²_res/n + V_g/M**, σ²_res = E Var(Y|Z), V_g = Var m(Z). For any fixed g, Var(h) = σ²_res + E(m−g)², so
  **excess over the floor = (1/n − 1/M)·E(m − g)², exactly** (Pythagoras). "Regular estimators cannot do better than V*" is the classical MCAR semiparametric-efficiency statement
  (Robins, Rotnitzky & Zhao, JASA 1994; Tsiatis, *Semiparametric Theory and Missing Data*, 2006 — cited for that half; not read in full by this role; the paper either cites it or gives a short proof).
- **PPI++ derived exactly** (scalar λ, g = λf, unlabeled-only averaging): V_{PPI++}(λ) = Var(Y−λf)/n + λ²Var(f)/N, minimised at λ* = Cov(Y,f)/[Var(f)(1+n/N)],
  value **V_{PPI++} = (Var(Y)/n)(1 − ρ²/(1+n/N))**, ρ = corr(Y,f). The pooled estimator with the best linear g = a*+b*f has *the same* variance (Var(h)=Var(Y)(1−ρ²) gives Var(Y)/n·[1 − ρ²(1 − n/M)], and 1−n/M = 1/(1+n/N)):
  PPI++ with tuned λ is the pooled linear estimator, with λ = b*·N/M. **Consequence: with λ tuned, the "pooled Z" step is already inside PPI++ and is worth exactly zero for linear g.**
  The free gain V_g(1/N − 1/M) belongs to λ=1 PPI (and to any mis-scaled g), i.e. to the PPI → PPI++ step. Exact excess of PPI++ over the floor:
  **V_{PPI++} − V* = (1/n − 1/M)·Δ, Δ = E(m(f) − a* − b*f)²** (best-linear-approximation gap of E[Y|f]). **No room iff Δ = 0, i.e. E[Y|f] is affine** (Gaussian synthetic case: closed form).
  The calibrated route is the same family with g = ĝ ≈ m and λ* = N/M (=1/(1+n/N)); it attains V* at ĝ = m.

## Submission process changes

- **Pending updates:** "ICML is planning to make some updates to the submission process (but not the submission format)." These are due to be announced by late November.
- **Two-stage review:** Area chairs screen papers first, and a senior area chair must confirm each early rejection. The page says "ICML 2027 will review submissions in two stages."
- **Contribution type:** Authors must pick one type: General, Theory, Application-driven, Concept and Feasibility, Negative Results, Datasets/Evaluations/Benchmarks, or Position. They should "select the Contribution Type that best reflects the primary scientific contribution".
- **Position papers:** These now go through the main track by choosing the Position Paper contribution type.
- **Submission caps and reciprocal reviewing:**
  - "No author may appear on more than 20 submissions."
  - Each submission needs one designated reciprocal reviewer, who can cover at most 6 submissions.
  - Authors with 3 or more submissions must also serve on the program committee.
  - "Submissions that do not meet these requirements will be desk rejected."
- **Self-rankings:** Authors with multiple submissions must rank their own papers, continuing the ICML 2026 practice.
- **Lay summaries:** Authors of accepted papers must submit one with the camera-ready version.
- **LLM use in reviewing:** There is now one policy. "Delegating judgement and critique of the paper to LLMs is not allowed".

## Page limit and format

- The limit is "8 pages for the main paper, with unlimited pages for references, the impact statement, and appendices."
- Papers are a single file, and there is no separate supplementary deadline.
- Camera-ready versions get "one extra page for the main paper."
- The submission format is stated to be unchanged. Authors must use the ICML 2027 style files, and nonconforming papers are rejected without review.

## Checklist and reproducibility

- The page doesn't mention a checklist.
- The reviewing criteria say claims must be "supported by reproducible experiments and/or sound theoretical analysis." This is not flagged as new.

## Impact statement

- This is still required, in a separate section near the end before the references, and it is outside the page limit.
- Papers with only standard societal implications can use the suggested boilerplate statement verbatim.
- Ethics reviewers may be asked to look at flagged papers.

## AI disclosure (new)

- Authors must disclose substantive generative AI use, such as ideation, code generation, data analysis, or heavy drafting. Routine grammar and formatting help is exempt.
- "All submissions must include an AI Disclosure Statement." It does not count toward the page limit.
- If generative AI is part of the method itself, the paper must describe it in enough detail to reproduce the work.

- The author list is fixed after the abstract deadline. Authors can be reordered but not added or removed.

- **Why ICML 2027:** it is the only edition that is both the newest and still open (full paper due Jan 22, 2027). ICLR 2027 is already in review, and NeurIPS 2026 is a year older with its deadlines past.
- **Limits:** the main text is 8 pages, two-column, US Letter, with 3.25 in columns and 6.75 in full width. References and appendices are unlimited.
- **Required sections:** there is no paper checklist. ICML instead requires an Impact Statement and an AI Disclosure Statement, both outside the page limit. The disclosure must say AI agents carried out the study.
- **Float budget:** at most 5 floats in the main text. I told `story-repo` to keep Fig 2, 3, 4, 6 and Table 1, and move Fig 1, Fig 5 and Tables 2–3 to the appendix.
- **How accepted papers are written:** I sampled 10 statistics-flavoured ICML 2024 papers (`venue.md` lists them), and the counts are by script, so treat them as roughly ±10%.

  - Main-text tables: 0–3 (median 0).
  - References: 22–85 (median about 43).

- **File-size limit:** the author instructions say 50 MB and the kit says 10 MB. I told the other roles to keep the PDF under 10 MB.
- **Reviewer guidance:** I did not read ICML's per-contribution-type guidance. I suggested "General" as the contribution type.
- **Submission-process updates:** ICML promised these by late November, and they had not appeared on 2026-11-26. I will re-check before a version is approved.
- **`venue-artifacts.json`:** I have not written it, because `.forgejo/CODEOWNERS` in `paper-repo` does not yet name any paths. I will add it once it does.
